test_title: PYST 24: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 19 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: Three candidates X, Y and Z participated in an election. X got 30% more votes than Y, whereas Z got 25% more votes than Y. X also overtook Z by 5000 votes. If 71% of the voters voted and no invalid votes were cast, then what was the total number of voters in the voting list?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Y = 100 units ⇒ X = 130 units and Z = 125 units.

Difference (X − Z) = 130 − 125 = 5 units → 5000 votes.

Total cast votes = X + Y + Z = 130 + 100 + 125 = 355 units.

Total cast votes = 355 × (5000 ÷ 5) = 3,55,000.

Total voters list = (3,55,000 ÷ 71) × 100 = 5,00,000.

**∴ The correct option is A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

X = 130% of Y, Z = 125% of Y, X − Z = 5000, Cast votes = 71% of Total list.

**Formula Used:**

Number of votes = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Base value; Total Voters = (Cast Votes ÷ Cast Percentage) × 100.

 
 Y (100u)
 
 Z (125u)
 
 X (130u)
 
• 
 
• 
 Diff = 5u
 5u = 5000
 
• 
 Total Votes Cast = X + Y + Z = 355 units

⇒ Let Y = 100u

⇒ X = 100u + 30% of 100u = 130u

⇒ Z = 100u + 25% of 100u = 125u

⇒ X − Z = 130u − 125u = 5u

⇒ 5u = 5000 ⇒ 1u = 1000

⇒ Total votes cast = 130u + 100u + 125u = 355u

⇒ Total votes cast = 355 × 1000 = 3,55,000

⇒ 71% of Total voters = 3,55,000

⇒ Total voters in list = (3,55,000 ÷ 71) × 100

⇒ Total voters in list = 5000 × 100 = 5,00,000

**∴ The correct option is A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Comparison

If A is x% more than B, then A = B × (1 + x/100). If A is x% less than B, then A = B × (1 − x/100).

Election Terminology

Voter List Total = Votes Polled + Non-voters. Votes Polled = Valid Votes + Invalid Votes.

Common Base Method

When multiple variables are compared to one common variable, assume the common variable as 100 to simplify calculations.</p
